question: to the Commission Piotr Müller (ECR) Subject:

The agreement (EMPA and iTA) between the EU and Mercosur was signed on 17 January 2026. The trade part of the agreement will be provisionally applied as from 1 May 2026. This is controversial as the European Parliament has suspended final approval of the agreement and referred it to the Court of Justice of the EU. Although the EU has recently adopted legislation which in theory will protect our agricultural sector, fundamental questions remain unanswered. Citizens and farmers still have serious and unresolved concerns about food safety, the hidden costs for the EU budget and the overall impact of the agreement on our agricultural economy. In light of the above: 1.
In view of the Commission’s announcement regarding the strengthening of sanitary and phytosanitary controls, what will be the specific procedures and scope of the new import control task force?

Will the planned EUR 6.3 billion crisis reserve for farmers, provided for under the future CAP budget for 2028-2034, be redeployed from other existing funding lines, and if so, from which ones exactly?

Is the Commission planning to have a comprehensive macroeconomic assessment carried out of the impact that the provisional application of the agreement will have, taking into account the effect on employment in regions dependent on agriculture, as well as on the EU’s GDP and trade balance, and to publish the results before the final vote in the European Parliament?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.6.2026) The Import Control Task Force1 does not replace official controls performed by Member States or create parallel structures, but builds on existing expert and working groups within the framework of import controls (namely, groups on veterinary import controls, food and feed of non-animal origin, plant health, e-commerce and the Official Controls Regulation2), bringing them together in a coordinated and strategic way. Its added value lies in improving harmonised implementation in the EU, identifying gaps or inconsistencies and proposing joint actions where an EU-level approach is best. The Unity safety net3, amounting to EUR 6.3 billion over the 2028-2034 period, will serve as a dedicated tool within the EU Facility to address market disturbances and ensure agricultural market stability. It replaces the current agricultural reserve, doubling its budget and supporting a stronger crisis response for farmers. The funding is integrated into the next Multiannual Financial Framework, without redeploying resources from other EU priorities. The Commission has already conducted an economic analysis of the negotiated outcome of the EU-Mercosur Partnership Agreement4, published in June 2025. This assesses the agreement’s projected impacts on key areas, including gross domestic product, trade flows, employment and sectoral effects, with particular attention to sensitive sectors such as agriculture. No further comprehensive macroeconomic assessment is planned specifically for the phase of the EU-Mercosur Interim Trade Agreement’s provisional application. The existing analysis, alongside ongoing monitoring, will inform stakeholders.
